# Receipt fixture boundary

These are synthetic fixtures generated by `node scripts/create-receipt-fixtures.mjs`. They contain no personal data. They do **not** establish support for any supermarket, language, OCR system, or AI model.

| File | Content | Verified use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| synthetic-text.pdf | Embedded text with rice multipack, weighted apples, milk, discount, and an ambiguous item | PDF structural validation, upload/hash identity and storage tests |
| synthetic-image-only.pdf | One stretched blank image, no embedded grocery text | Valid image-only PDF input; no extraction accuracy claim |
| proposal.json | Hand-authored expected example proposal, including unresolved quantity | Contract validation only; never returned by production parsing |

A user supplied one German REWE eBon on 2026-10-25. The original stays outside Git; payment, loyalty, store and fiscal identifiers are not committed. Both pages have embedded text, and a private local extraction check preserved all 33 priced source labels. This measures text preservation, not product interpretation or model accuracy. Model integration is implemented but disabled without server key/model configuration. Before enabling it, collect sanitized digital and scanned examples, choose/evaluate an embedded-text parser and a model, test the shared two-call/time budget and stale-attempt leases, and measure line coverage and field accuracy. The image-only fixture is not an OCR quality benchmark. PDFs requiring an opening password are rejected. Owner-protected PDFs that open without a password (such as this sample, which permits copying) are accepted.

## REWE-style regression fixtures

`rewe-style-fictional.pdf` is a new fictional two-page PDF built by `scripts/create-rewe-fixture.mjs`. It retains representative layout patterns but changes purchase details and omits all real identifiers. `rewe-style-expected.json` is manually annotated expected review evidence, not model output. It covers weighted bananas/chestnuts, repeated item counts, missing milk carton size, explicit bottle size, deposits, a discount and ambiguous/non-food labels. It never assumes a package size or unknown purchase count.

`rewe-style-readable-protected.pdf` reproduces the password-free, owner-protected behavior. `password-required.pdf` requires the test-only opening password `fixture-opening-password` and must be rejected by the app. Regenerate these with `python3 scripts/create-protected-fixtures.py` using pypdf 6.10.0; ordinary tests use the committed fictional files and do not require Python. The owner password is test data, not a credential.

The initial unpdf 1.9.1/PDF.js 6.4.299 extractor preserves all expected labels and quantity evidence. Sparse, garbled, partly empty and oversized extracted text is routed to `vision_required`; vision/model execution is now implemented behind configuration, with mocked execution tests. The blank image fixture only proves no-text routing. A single digital REWE sample does not establish scanned receipt support, universal German parsing, or complete receipt acceptance.

`rewe-model-proposal.json` is hand-authored mocked model output for the fictional receipt. It preserves all nine priced labels and deliberately leaves unknown carton/package sizes unresolved. It is used only by unit tests and explicitly enabled test-only handlers, never by the production parser. It does not describe an actual model response. Tests exercise source-order coverage, text/PDF routing, bounded fallback/retries, refusals, malformed/oversized responses, and real backend draft/stock confirmation. Scanned-receipt quality and paid model evaluation are still unverified.
